turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CAREGIVER): Sorry doctor, we are a little late only. The auto was stuck near the market, and then the lift was not working.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): That is quite alright, please sit, both of you. The rain has made every road a bit mad today, hasn't it.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes doctor. Thank you for seeing us even so. We are grateful.
[SEG0004] person_4 (NURSE): I will just do the temperature and the rest before you both start. One small minute.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CAREGIVER): While she does that, my own sister is down with fever at my place. She is finishing her strip of Crocin, for herself. Nothing to do with him.
[SEG0006] person_4 (NURSE): Right. Temperature is 37.8 celsius. Pulse 96. Blood pressure 118 over 76. Oxygen 98 percent. Breathing 18.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you, sister. Rohan, tell me in your own words, what brought you in today?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): Doctor, the bone pains have come back. That is why I came.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am sorry. Where is it sitting, and for how long now?
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): umm, both the thighs, and the lower back also. I was going to say three days, no, sorry, it is two days. It is quite bad when I walk.
[SEG0011] person_1 (CAREGIVER): He was holding the wall this morning, doctor. He did not want to come out of the bed at all.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever along with this?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes doctor. A mild fever since yesterday evening. I feel a bit tired also.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain, or trouble with the breathing?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No doctor. No chest pain, and the breathing is normal.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the urine? Any dark colour, or are you passing less?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Urine is a normal colour, doctor. I am passing it as usual.
[SEG0018] person_4 (NURSE): My own boy gets knee pain every monsoon, so I always notice the weather. It has been very damp, no?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes sister, it has been raining. But this pain feels like my usual sickle pain, not only the weather.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): You have sickle cell disease, isn't it. It is there on the old notes. Since when, roughly?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes doctor. Since childhood. I am also followed at the government hospital.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the regular medicines, are you taking them?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes doctor. The folic acid tablet, five milligrams, every morning. And haidrea, I mean Hydrea, the yellow capsule, 500 milligrams at night.

[SEG0024] person_1 (CAREGIVER): I keep his strip in the kitchen box, and he has been regular this month. My sister's biotin tablets are in that same box, those are hers, for the hair. I must not mix them.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you already taken any pain tablet for this?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): No doctor. I have not taken any painkiller yet.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to a medicine, that you know of?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): No doctor. There is no allergy to any medicine.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me press gently. Both thighs are tender. The muscles of the lower back are a bit tight. The chest is clear, and I do not see a rash.
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): It does hurt when you press, doctor. I am sorry.

[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): No need to be sorry. In sickle cell the red cells bend into a sickle shape and they clog the small vessels inside the bone. That blockage is what brings this deep pain. It is not an injury from outside.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): My impression is a mild vaso-occlusive pain episode, with this low grade fever. I do not think this is an acute chest crisis.
[SEG0033] person_1 (CAREGIVER): Will you admit him, doctor? I have my own evening shift at the shop, so I need to know.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): I do not think we need admission today, if he can drink and the blood tests are alright. We will do a blood count, a reticulocyte count, and a fever screen, the CRP.
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): Kindly tell me what I should do at home, doctor.

[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Drink plenty of fluids, about three litres through the day, warm water is fine, and rest the legs. I will also start Crocin, six hundred and fifty milligrams, three times a day after food, for three days, for the pain and the fever.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): Should I continue the Hydrea and the folic acid tablet as before?
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, please continue both. Do not stop them. Hydrea stays 500 milligrams at night, and folic acid five milligrams in the morning.
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): If the tiredness increases a little, is that something to worry about?

[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): A little tiredness can come with the fever itself. If the pain becomes severe, or the breathing gets difficult, or the fever crosses 101, come straight to emergency. Otherwise I will see you in three days with the reports.
[SEG0041] person_4 (NURSE): I can take the blood sample now, before you leave. The lab is open till four.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes please, sister. Send a full blood count, a retic count, and CRP today.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): Three days is quite alright, doctor. Thank you for explaining.
[SEG0044] person_1 (CAREGIVER): I will see that he drinks. At my house the water filter is very slow, that is my own headache, we will manage.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Collect the Crocin from the pharmacy on the way out. Take care, Rohan.
[SEG0046] person_4 (NURSE): Sit just outside. I will call you in two minutes for the sample.

spec.situation: Young adult with known sickle cell disease and bone pains for two days, fever mild; takes folic acid and hydroxyurea; fluids and painkiller plan; blood tests planned.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

bad.reason: Tiredness is reported present, but transcript does not state it is mild.
bad.text: Tiredness (category=constitutional, status=present, severity=mild, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)
